title: Cohomological bound for a derived functor on unbounded complexes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be an additive functor on the category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which commutes with countable direct products, and let $N\ge0$ be an integer. Suppose $R^pF(\mathcal F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and every $p\ge N$, where $RF$ and $R^pF$ are the right derived functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. If $b$ is an integer and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] has $H^i(E)=0$ for $i>b$, then $H^i(RF(E))=0$ for $i>b+N-1$.

proof.text: For each n\ge0 put E_n=\tau_{\ge -n}E. The truncation tower reconstruction and the compatibility of the right derived functor with its derived inverse limit give E\simeq R\varprojlim_nE_n and RF(E)\simeq R\varprojlim_nRF(E_n) by [lem-pc-qcoh-truncation-derived-limit].

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), first paragraph; Tags 08D3 and 08D1

proof.text: Applying the Milnor exact sequence [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] to the tower RF(E_n), for every i we obtain $$0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{i-1}(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E))\to\varprojlim_n H^i(RF(E_n))\to0.$$

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), displayed short exact sequence; Tag 07KY

proof.text: The shifted truncation triangle and the vanishing hypothesis give the stabilization statement [lem-pc-derived-functor-truncation-stabilization]: H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1})) is an isomorphism whenever n\ge N-i, because the two endpoint cohomology groups are R^{i+n}F(H^{-n}(E)) and R^{i+n+1}F(H^{-n}(E)).

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), truncation triangle and the two shifted derived-functor vanishings

proof.text: Fix $i$. By Step 3 (applied in degrees $i$ and $i-1$) the transition maps of the towers $H^{i-1}(RF(E_n))$ and $H^i(RF(E_n))$ are isomorphisms for $n\ge N-i+1$ and $n\ge N-i$ respectively. An eventually constant tower of abelian groups is Mittag--Leffler, so its $R^1\varprojlim$ vanishes, and its limit maps isomorphically to each term past the stabilization index (Stacks Tag 07KW). Hence the left term of the sequence of Step 2 is zero and $H^i(RF(E))\cong H^i(RF(E_m))$ for every integer $m\ge\max(0,N-i-1)$.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), Mittag--Leffler conclusion; More on Algebra Tag 07KW

proof.text: Let $i>b+N-1$, i.e. $i\ge b+N$, and put $m=\max(0,N-i-1)$; then $m\ge -b-1$ since $N-i-1\le -b-1$. Every integer $n$ with $-b\le n\le m$ satisfies $n\ge -b\ge N-i$, so by [lem-pc-derived-functor-truncation-stabilization] the maps $H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))$ for $n=m,m-1,\dots,-b$ are isomorphisms, and their composite gives $H^i(RF(E_m))\cong H^i(RF(E_{-b-1}))=H^i(RF(\tau_{\ge b+1}E))$. Since $H^j(E)=0$ for $j>b$, $\tau_{\ge b+1}E=0$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and $RF(0)=0$. With Step 4, $H^i(RF(E))=0$ for every $i>b+N-1$.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (3), final paragraph
